mainTopic: Whether a hide cancels attached flesh (רב הונא), and the משנה of skins that count like their flesh: human skin, pig skin, and young camels and calves.
overview: Just before this amud, רב הונא taught that flesh left on a hide is cancelled out (בטל) by the hide. The גמרא asks which תנא he follows: רבי ישמעאל, who says the hide does not cancel the flesh, or רבי עקיבא, who says it does. At first the גמרא says he follows רבי ישמעאל, who it says only meant flesh left by an animal and not by a knife. It drops that answer because of רב הונא's comment on רבי יהודה about gathered scraps. It concludes that רב הונא follows רבי עקיבא, and his חידוש is that the hide cancels the flesh however it was left. Then a new משנה lists skins that count like their flesh, such as human skin, pig skin and soft young skins, and says tanning makes them pure, except human skin. עולא says human skin is pure by Torah law and impure only by a גזירה, and the גמרא gives two versions of where his statement belongs. The גמרא then explains the argument about the wild boar's skin and defines a 'young' camel, adding two short stories about ריש לקיש and רבי זירא. It then begins defining a 'young' calf, a discussion that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Whose opinion is רב הונא following?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא רב הונא's ruling about flesh on the hide matches.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to whom?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which תנא stands behind רב הונא's ruling that flesh stuck to the hide is cancelled out. This short question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known מחלוקת between רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא about whether a hide cancels out flesh attached to it. The גמרא wants to place רב הונא on one side of that argument.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom? Which opinion does this follow?

phrases.english: According to whom?
phrases.notes: Whose opinion is רב הונא's ruling (just before this) following?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens an inquiry into the source of רב הונא's earlier statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא, רבי ישמעאל or רבי עקיבא, רב הונא's ruling matches.

steps.title: Neither option seems to work
steps.stepSummary: If רב הונא follows רבי ישמעאל, he contradicts him. If he follows רבי עקיבא, his ruling is obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it follows רבי ישמעאל, but he said the hide does not cancel out the flesh! And if it follows רבי עקיבא, it is obvious, since he said the hide does cancel it out!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that both possible answers cause a problem. With רבי ישמעאל, רב הונא contradicts him. With רבי עקיבא, רב הונא adds nothing new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה on 124a, רבי ישמעאל says flesh attached to a hide is not cancelled by it, so it can still make a person טמא through carrying. רבי עקיבא says the hide does cancel it out. רב הונא said the flesh is בטל, which clashes with רבי ישמעאל and simply repeats רבי עקיבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Cancels out, makes something count as part of something else

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two sides: רבי ישמעאל = the hide does NOT cancel the flesh. רבי עקיבא = the hide DOES cancel it.

phrases.english: If it is according to רבי ישמעאל –
but he said the hide does not cancel out [the flesh]!
phrases.notes: This refers to the משנה on 124a about a hide with flesh stuck to it.

phrases.english: And if it is according to רבי עקיבא –
it is obvious, since he said the hide does cancel it out!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל הָאָמַר לֹא מְבַטֵּל עוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the question into a challenge from both sides.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling that flesh left on the hide is בטל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Following רבי ישמעאל contradicts him. Following רבי עקיבא makes the ruling unnecessary.

steps.title: רב הונא follows רבי ישמעאל: a knife is different from an animal
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל only said the hide doesn't cancel flesh left by an animal. Flesh left by a knife is cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really it follows רבי ישמעאל. When רבי ישמעאל said the hide does not cancel out the flesh, that is only where an animal left it. But where a knife left it, it is cancelled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב הונא does follow רבי ישמעאל. רבי ישמעאל's rule was only about a specific kind of case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא splits the cases. Flesh left on the hide by an animal is not בטל, and that is רבי ישמעאל's case. Flesh left by a knife while skinning is בטל, and that is רב הונא's case. So רב הונא adds something new and does not contradict רבי ישמעאל.

keyTerms.meaning: Left it behind, peeled it off

steps.whatToRemember: For now, the גמרא suggests that according to רבי ישמעאל, flesh left by an animal is not בטל to the hide, but flesh left by a knife is בטל. Step 6 drops this answer.

phrases.english: Really, it is according to רבי ישמעאל,

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל לֹא מְבַטֵּל עוֹר –
phrases.english: and when רבי ישמעאל said the hide does not cancel out [the flesh] –
that is only where an animal left it [on the hide],
but if a knife left it – it is cancelled out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by narrowing רבי ישמעאל's ruling.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): animal versus knife
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי ישמעאל holds the hide never cancels attached flesh.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי ישמעאל only means flesh left by an animal. Flesh left by a knife is בטל, which is רב הונא's case.

steps.title: A new source: רבי יהודה on collected flesh scraps
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רבי יהודה's rule about gathered scraps of flesh (אלל) and רב הונא's comment that someone must have gathered them, to start a challenge.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי יהודה says, collected scraps of flesh, if there is an olive's worth in one place, one is liable for it. And רב הונא said: only when he collected it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source to test the answer it just gave about רב הונא. This step sets up the challenge, which Step 5 spells out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה says scraps of flesh left on a hide, once gathered into one olive-sized amount, carry טומאת נבלה and bring liability. רב הונא adds that this applies only when a person actually gathered them. The גמרא will use this to question how רב הונא views flesh on the hide.

keyTerms.meaning: Scraps of flesh left stuck to the hide after skinning
An olive's worth, the minimum amount for טומאת נבלה

phrases.english: Come and hear: רבי יהודה says:
collected scraps of flesh,
if there is an olive's worth in one place –
one is liable for it,
phrases.notes: Liable for becoming טמא from it and then eating קדשים or entering the מקדש.

phrases.english: And רב הונא said: and that is when he collected it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: הָאָלָל הַמְכוּנָּס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new source to test the explanation given in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that רב הונא follows רבי ישמעאל, with flesh left by a knife being בטל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב הונא's comment on רבי יהודה's rule about gathered flesh scraps will be weighed against this view. The full challenge is spelled out in Step 5.

steps.title: If the knife-flesh is cancelled for רבי ישמעאל, whose view is רב הונא's scraps comment?
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא's comment about gathered scraps treats knife-left flesh as not cancelled. That fits רבי ישמעאל only if he holds knife-flesh is not cancelled. Under Step 3's answer, where he holds it is cancelled, whom does רב הונא follow?
steps.simpleTranslation: It works if רבי ישמעאל also holds that flesh left by a knife is not cancelled, because then רב הונא's comment matches רבי ישמעאל. But if רבי ישמעאל holds that knife-flesh is cancelled, then whose view is רב הונא's comment?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge it set up in Step 4. It attacks the answer from Step 3, which said that for רבי ישמעאל flesh left by a knife is cancelled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא said someone must have gathered the scraps. That means the flesh left by the knife still counts and is not cancelled by the hide. If רבי ישמעאל really held that knife-flesh is cancelled, רב הונא's comment would have no תנא to stand on.

keyTerms.meaning: It works out fine / granted (the first half of a 'this works, but that doesn't' challenge)
A knife left it (flesh left on the hide while skinning with a knife)
Is cancelled. The flesh becomes part of the hide and loses its own status.
Like whom? (Which תנא does this follow?)

phrases.english: It works if you say that where a knife left the flesh,
according to Rabbi Yishmael too it is not cancelled,
then Rav Huna, who said it, said it like Rabbi Yishmael.
phrases.notes: This is רב הונא's comment from the last step, that someone gathered the scraps, which treats the flesh as still counting.

phrases.english: But if you say that where a knife left the flesh,
according to Rabbi Yishmael it is cancelled,
then Rav Huna, who said it, follows whom?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge that Step 4 began setting up.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 3's answer that, for רבי ישמעאל, flesh left by a knife is cancelled.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב הונא's scraps comment assumes knife-flesh is not cancelled. If רבי ישמעאל held it is cancelled, and רבי עקיבא holds all flesh is cancelled, no תנא supports רב הונא's comment.

steps.title: Even knife-flesh is not cancelled for רבי ישמעאל, so רב הונא follows רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops Step 3's answer. For רבי ישמעאל, even flesh left by a knife is not cancelled. רב הונא's ruling that the hide cancels the flesh follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, really, flesh left by a knife is not cancelled according to רבי ישמעאל, and רב הונא's ruling follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up the answer from Step 3 and goes back to a simpler picture. רבי ישמעאל says the flesh is not cancelled, and רב הונא's ruling that the hide cancels it matches רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now רב הונא's scraps comment fits רבי ישמעאל, since knife-flesh is not cancelled there. His main ruling, that the hide cancels the flesh, fits רבי עקיבא. But this brings back the problem from Step 2: if he follows רבי עקיבא, why did he need to say it?

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (we drop the earlier answer and replace it)
Really / actually (we go back to the plain understanding)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two comments of רב הונא. The scraps comment matches רבי ישמעאל (flesh not cancelled). His main ruling that the hide cancels the flesh matches רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: Rather, really, where a knife left the flesh,
according to Rabbi Yishmael it is not cancelled,
and Rav Huna said his ruling like Rabbi Akiva!
phrases.notes: Here it means רב הונא's main ruling (the one Step 1 asked about), that the hide cancels the flesh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 5 by dropping Step 3's answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Retracting the earlier answer and assigning רב הונא's ruling to a different תנא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: For רבי ישמעאל, knife-flesh is cancelled and רב הונא follows him (Step 3).
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי ישמעאל, even knife-flesh is not cancelled. רב הונא's ruling follows רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: If רב הונא follows רבי עקיבא, his ruling is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks again: if רב הונא follows רבי עקיבא, why did he need to say anything?
steps.simpleTranslation: That's obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back the challenge from Step 2. If רבי עקיבא already said the hide cancels the flesh, רב הונא added nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אמורא is not supposed to just repeat what a תנא already said. Now that רב הונא's ruling is tied to רבי עקיבא, the גמרא needs to show what new thing he teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: It's obvious! (Why did he need to say it?)

phrases.english: That's obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the result of Step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 6's claim that רב הונא follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי עקיבא already said the hide cancels the flesh, so רב הונא's ruling seems to teach nothing new.

steps.title: רב הונא teaches that רבי עקיבא's rule covers flesh left by an animal too
steps.stepSummary: We might have thought רבי עקיבא spoke only about flesh left by a knife. רב הונא teaches that even flesh left by an animal is cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that when רבי עקיבא said the hide cancels the flesh, that was only for flesh left by a knife, but flesh left by an animal is not cancelled. So רב הונא teaches that it is cancelled too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers why רב הונא needed to speak. His ruling stops us from limiting רבי עקיבא's rule to knife-flesh.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wild animal tearing off the hide is a different case from skinning with a knife. We might have thought רבי עקיבא's rule did not reach it. רב הונא's ruling makes רבי עקיבא's rule apply to both cases, so his statement is not just a repeat.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces the mistaken idea that the ruling comes to prevent)
This applies only (to a certain case)
An animal left it (flesh left on the hide when a wild animal tore it off)

steps.whatToRemember: In the end: רבי ישמעאל holds the hide does not cancel the flesh, even flesh left by a knife. רבי עקיבא holds it does. רב הונא follows רבי עקיבא and adds that this applies even to flesh left by an animal.

phrases.english: You might have said,
when Rabbi Akiva said it,
that applies only where a knife left the flesh,
but where an animal left it, it is not cancelled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge of Step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing what is new: the ruling widens רבי עקיבא's rule to another case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא's rule covers only flesh left by a knife, and flesh left by an animal is not cancelled.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי עקיבא, the hide cancels the flesh whether a knife or an animal left it.

steps.title: רב הונא's חידוש: the hide cancels no matter how the flesh was left
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא teaches that רבי עקיבא's reason is that the hide cancels the flesh. This works the same whether an animal or a knife left the flesh.
steps.simpleTranslation: He teaches us that רבי עקיבא's reason is that the hide cancels the bits of flesh. So it makes no difference whether an animal tore it or a knife cut it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer from Step 8. It explains exactly what רב הונא added by speaking up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might have thought רבי עקיבא only spoke about flesh left by a knife. רב הונא points to the reason behind the rule: the hide itself cancels the flesh. Since the reason has nothing to do with how the flesh got there, the rule applies to flesh left by an animal too.

keyTerms.meaning: He teaches us (the new point being made)
Cancels them (makes the small bits of flesh lose their own status)

phrases.english: He teaches us
that the reason of Rabbi Akiva
is because the hide cancels them,
no difference whether an animal tore it away
phrases.notes: Some versions have the short word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording we read.

phrases.english: and no difference whether a knife cut it away.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer begun in Step 8 by stating what רב הונא teaches.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing a new point (חידוש) that justifies the statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא's rule might apply only to flesh left by a knife.
steps.terutzMaskana: The hide cancels the flesh in every case, whether an animal or a knife left it.

steps.title: Support from the end of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רב הונא's point matches the end of the משנה, which gives the hide as רבי עקיבא's reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is just what the end of the משנה teaches: Why does רבי עקיבא rule pure when there is a hide? Because the hide cancels the bits of flesh.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports רב הונא's reading by quoting the last part of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה itself states that רבי עקיבא's reason is that the hide cancels the flesh. Because the reason is the hide, and not the way the flesh was cut, רב הונא is right that the rule covers every case.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part of a משנה or ברייתא

steps.whatToRemember: The final word in this סוגיא: רב הונא follows רבי עקיבא. The hide cancels the leftover flesh whether an animal or a knife left it, as the end of the משנה says.

phrases.english: As the last part teaches:
For what reason does Rabbi Akiva
rule pure in the case of the hide?
Because the hide cancels them.
phrases.notes: "Them" means the small bits of flesh stuck to the hide.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support from the משנה for the point made in Step 9.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי עקיבא's reason is the hide itself, so it applies however the flesh was left.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The end of the משנה: מִפְּנֵי מָה רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מְטַהֵר בְּעוֹר.

steps.title: New משנה: skins that count like their flesh
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה begins its list of skins that are treated like flesh: a person's skin and a domestic pig's skin. רבי יהודה adds the wild boar.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: These are the ones whose skin counts like their flesh: a person's skin and the skin of a domestic pig. רבי יהודה says: the skin of a wild boar too.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. It lists cases where the skin has the same טומאה status as the flesh.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually skin is a separate thing from flesh. Here, though, some skins are soft or are eaten, so they count as flesh. The domestic pig's skin is soft. רבי יהודה holds the wild boar's skin also counts as flesh.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (marks the start of a new משנה)
A domestic pig, one raised where people live

phrases.english: MISHNA:
These are the ones whose skins are like their flesh:
the skin of a person,
and the skin of a domestic pig.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אַף עוֹר חֲזִיר הַבָּר.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: even the skin of a wild boar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the previous sugya closed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person's skin and a domestic pig's skin count like their flesh. רבי יהודה adds the wild boar's skin.

steps.title: More skins on the list, including four creeping creatures
steps.stepSummary: The משנה goes on with soft young skins and the skins of four שרצים. רבי יהודה disagrees about the lizard.
steps.simpleTranslation: Also on the list: the skin of a young camel's hump, the skin of a young calf's head, the skin of the hooves, the skin of the womb, the skin of a fetus, the skin under the tail fat, and the skin of the gecko, the monitor lizard, the lizard and the skink. רבי יהודה says: the lizard is like the weasel.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה keeps listing skins that count like flesh.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most of these skins are soft or tender, so they are treated like flesh. Four of the eight שרצים also have skin that counts like their flesh. רבי יהודה holds that the lizard belongs with the weasel, whose skin does not count like its flesh.

keyTerms.meaning: The fatty tail of a sheep
Weasel, one of the eight שרצים

phrases.english: And the skin of the hump of a young camel,
and the skin of the head of a young calf,
and the skin of the hooves, and the skin of the womb,

phrases.aramaic: וָעוֹר הַשְּׁלִיל, וְעוֹר שֶׁל תַּחַת הָאַלְיָה,
phrases.english: and the skin of a fetus, and the skin under the tail,
and the skin of the gecko, and the monitor lizard,
and the lizard, and the skink.
phrases.notes: These are four of the eight שרצים listed in ויקרא 11:29–30.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: the lizard is like the weasel.
phrases.notes: He means the lizard's skin does not count like its flesh, just as with the weasel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list started in Step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Soft young skins and the skins of four שרצים count like flesh. רבי יהודה takes the lizard off the list.

steps.title: Tanning makes these skins pure, except human skin
steps.stepSummary: If any of these skins is tanned, or walked on long enough to be tanned, it becomes pure. Human skin is the exception.
steps.simpleTranslation: All of them, if a person tanned them or walked on them long enough to tan them, are pure, except for human skin.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a rule that applies to the whole list it just gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tanning turns these skins into real leather, so they no longer count as flesh and become pure. Human skin is different. It keeps the status of flesh even after tanning.
steps.confusionAlert: Tanning does not help for human skin. It keeps the status of flesh even after being tanned.

phrases.english: And all of them, if one tanned them,
or walked on them long enough to tan them,
are pure, except for the skin of a person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a rule that applies to everything listed in Steps 11–12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Tanned skins on the list become pure, except human skin.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן בן נורי: all eight creeping creatures have real skins
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן בן נורי holds that all eight שרצים have real skins that do not count like their flesh.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן בן נורי says: the eight שרצים all have skins.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with רבי יוחנן בן נורי's opinion about the שרצים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion said that the skin of four שרצים counts like flesh. רבי יוחנן בן נורי disagrees. He holds that all eight have real skins that are separate from the flesh.

keyTerms.meaning: Creeping creatures; here, the eight that make things טמא when dead
Skins, meaning real skins that do not count as flesh

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri says:
The eight creeping creatures have skins.
phrases.notes: He means their skin is not counted like their flesh, so even the four on the list are not like flesh.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי אוֹמֵר שְׁמוֹנָה שְׁרָצִים יֵשׁ לָהֶן עוֹרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with Step 12, which put four שרצים on the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All eight שרצים have real skins that do not count like their flesh.

steps.title: עולא: human skin is pure by Torah law, impure only by decree
steps.stepSummary: עולא says a person's skin is pure by Torah law. The חכמים called it impure so people would not make mats from their parents' skins.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: עולא says: by Torah law a person's skin is pure. So why did the חכמים say it is impure? It is a גזירה, so that a person will not make mats out of his father's and mother's skins.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with עולא, who explains the first line of the משנה: a person's skin is treated like flesh. He says this is only a rabbinic rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said human skin counts like flesh, so it carries the טומאה of a dead body. עולא says the Torah itself does not make it impure. The חכמים added the טומאה as a fence, so that no one would treat a dead parent's skin as useful material.

keyTerms.meaning: By Torah law, as opposed to a rule of the חכמים
A protective decree the חכמים made to keep people from doing something wrong
Mats or rugs spread out on the ground
The skin of a human being

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Ulla says:
By Torah law, the skin of a person is pure,
phrases.notes: He means the skin of a dead person. That is the case the משנה is talking about.

phrases.english: and what is the reason they said it is impure?
It is a decree, lest a person make
the skins of his father and mother into mats.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא: דְּבַר תּוֹרָה עוֹר אָדָם טָהוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא on the new משנה by explaining its first ruling, that human skin is like flesh.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By Torah law human skin is pure. Its טומאה is a rabbinic גזירה, made so that people will not turn a parent's skin into mats.
steps.whyThisMatters: This tells us whether the טומאה of human skin is דאורייתא or דרבנן, and that question drives the rest of this section.

steps.title: Second version: עולא's statement applies only to tanned human skin
steps.stepSummary: Some place עולא's statement on the end of the משנה. In that version only tanned human skin is pure by Torah law, and the חכמים made it impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some teach עולא's statement on the end clause of the משנה: 'All of these skins, if one tanned them or walked on them long enough to tan them, are pure, except a person's skin.' On that, עולא says: by Torah law a person's skin that was tanned is pure. So why did the חכמים say it is impure? It is a גזירה, so that a person will not make mats out of his father's and mother's skins.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of where עולא's statement belongs. Here it is attached to the סיפא, about tanned skins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, עולא was talking about plain, untanned human skin. In this version he only talks about human skin that has already been tanned. The reason, the mats גזירה, stays the same, but the statement now covers less.

keyTerms.meaning: And there are those who teach it differently. This introduces a second version
The end clause of a משנה
Tanned them, meaning processed the hide into leather
The amount of time it takes to tan a hide

phrases.english: And there are those who teach it on the end clause:
"And all of them that one tanned
or walked on them long enough for tanning
are pure, except for a person's skin."
Ulla says:

phrases.aramaic: דְּבַר תּוֹרָה עוֹר אָדָם שֶׁעִבְּדוֹ טָהוֹר,
phrases.english: By Torah law, a person's skin that one tanned is pure,
and what is the reason they said it is impure?
It is a decree, lest a person make
the skins of his father and mother into mats.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of step 15, placing עולא's statement on the משנה's end clause.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only tanned human skin is pure by Torah law. Its טומאה is a rabbinic גזירה because of the mats concern.

steps.title: How the two versions differ in practice
steps.stepSummary: If עולא was talking about the רישא, he would say the same about the סיפא even more. If he was only talking about the סיפא, untanned human skin stays impure by Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who teaches עולא's statement on the first clause would say it even more so on the end clause. But the one who teaches it on the end clause holds that on the first clause, the טומאה is from the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא compares the two versions. It shows what each one means for untanned human skin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Untanned skin is closer to flesh than tanned skin is. So if even untanned skin is pure by Torah law, tanned skin is surely pure too. The second version only says this about tanned skin, so untanned human skin remains impure מדאורייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: The first clause of a משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up which version says more. The רישא version is the broader one: it makes even untanned skin pure by Torah law. The סיפא version is narrower, so untanned human skin stays truly impure.
steps.whatToRemember: Both versions agree that tanned human skin is pure by Torah law and impure only by גזירה. They argue only about untanned human skin.

phrases.english: The one who teaches it on the first clause,
all the more so on the end clause;
but the one who teaches it on the end clause,
but on the first clause, the impurity is from the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּמַתְנֵי לַהּ אַרֵישָׁא, כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן אַסֵּיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sums up the practical difference between the versions in steps 15 and 16.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Under the רישא version, all human skin is pure by Torah law. Under the סיפא version, only tanned human skin is, and untanned human skin is impure מדאורייתא.

steps.title: What is the argument about the wild boar's skin?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a pig's skin. It asks what the תנא קמא and רבי יהודה are really arguing about.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And the skin of a pig, etc.' What are they arguing about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה. It asks for the reason behind the argument over a wild boar's skin, and this sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא listed only a domestic pig's skin as counting like flesh. רבי יהודה added the wild boar. The גמרא wants to know what idea divides them.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc. The rest of the quoted line

phrases.english: "And the skin of a pig, etc."
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording. It just points to the rest of the משנה's line.

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the human-skin topic and turns to the pig-skin argument in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What reasoning separates the תנא קמא and רבי יהודה about the wild boar's skin.

steps.title: Tough or soft: the wild boar's skin
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא holds that a wild boar's skin is tough, unlike a domestic pig's soft skin. רבי יהודה holds the wild boar's skin is soft too.
steps.simpleTranslation: One חכם holds: this one (the wild boar) is tough and that one (the domestic pig) is soft. The other חכם holds: this one is also soft.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the argument is about a fact: how soft a wild boar's skin is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Soft skin is treated like flesh, and tough skin is not. The תנא קמא thinks a חזיר הבר has tough skin, so it does not count like flesh. רבי יהודה thinks it is just as soft as a domestic pig's skin, so it does count like flesh.

keyTerms.meaning: One חכם holds... The way the גמרא lays out two opinions side by side

steps.whatToRemember: The rule underneath this argument: soft skin counts like flesh, and tough skin does not.

phrases.english: One Sage holds:
this one is tough
phrases.notes: "This one" is the wild boar. This is the view of the תנא קמא.

phrases.english: and that one is soft,
and the other Sage holds:
this one is also soft.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר סָבַר: הַאי אַשּׁוּן וְהַאי רַכִּיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The two opinions disagree about a fact: whether a wild boar's skin is tough, as the תנא קמא holds, or soft like a domestic pig's skin, as רבי יהודה holds.

steps.title: Until when is a camel called young?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of a young camel's hump-skin and asks how long a camel counts as 'young'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: the skin of the hump of a young camel. How long is a camel considered young?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from the משנה and asks for a definition. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a young camel's hump-skin is treated like meat, because it is still soft. But the משנה never says what 'young' means. The גמרא wants a clear cutoff point.

keyTerms.meaning: A young camel, literally 'a tender camel'

phrases.english: The skin of the hump of a young camel
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה, which treats this soft skin like the meat itself.

phrases.english: And until when is a camel considered young?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the pig-skin case in the משנה to the next case, the camel's hump.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The age or stage at which a camel stops being 'young' for this law.

steps.title: Young means it has not yet carried a load
steps.stepSummary: עולא in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי says a camel is young as long as it has not carried a load.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי: as long as it has not carried a load.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: the camel is 'young' until it has carried a load.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The cutoff is not a number of years but a real-life event: carrying loads. Once a camel carries loads, its hump-skin is understood to have hardened into true skin.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר עוּלָּא, אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי:
phrases.english: Ulla said that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
As long as it has not carried a load.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא, אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A camel is young as long as it has not carried a load.

steps.title: Old enough to carry, but never carried
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks about a camel old enough to carry loads that has not actually carried any.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה asked: if the camel reached the age to carry but did not carry, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה tests the rule with a borderline case: the age has come, but no load was carried.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He wants to know what the rule really depends on. Is it the actual carrying, or the age when camels normally start carrying? If it is the age, this camel is no longer young.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked a question he was unsure of

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya asked:
If its time to carry a load has come
but it has not carried, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the rule of step 21 on an edge case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether reaching carrying age alone ends the 'young' status.

steps.title: Carried a load before its time
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks the opposite case: a camel too young to carry that carried anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי asked: if the camel was not old enough to carry but did carry, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי asks the mirror-image case of רבי ירמיה's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the camel actually carried, but it was still too young by age. Does the early carrying already make its skin hard and end its 'young' status, or does age decide?

keyTerms.meaning: Its time has not yet come

phrases.english: Abaye asked:
If its time to carry a load has not come
but it did carry, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks the reverse of רבי ירמיה's case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether actually carrying early ends the 'young' status even before the normal age.

steps.title: Both questions stay unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends both questions with תיקו: they remain unanswered.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let them stand unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes both questions without an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No source decides whether age or actual carrying is what counts. So both borderline cases stay in doubt.
steps.whatToRemember: A camel is 'young' until it carries a load. But if age and carrying do not match, the law is left in doubt (תיקו).

phrases.english: Let it stand unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the two questions of steps 22 and 23.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The two edge cases remain in doubt.

steps.title: ריש לקיש asks the same question
steps.stepSummary: A story: ריש לקיש sat and wondered how long a camel counts as young.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש was sitting and wondering: until when is a camel young?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a short story where ריש לקיש asks the same question from step 20. This sets up the answer he gets.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is asked here. The story shows how the teaching of רבי יהושע בן לוי was passed on to other great sages.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish was sitting and wondering:
Until when is a camel considered young?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a story repeating the question of step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The definition of a young camel.

steps.title: ריש לקיש is answered and honors the answerer
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל בר אבא tells ריש לקיש the teaching of רבי יהושע בן לוי, and ריש לקיש invites him to sit facing him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל בר אבא said to him: this is what רבי יהושע בן לוי said, as long as it has not carried a load. ריש לקיש said to him: sit facing me.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gets the same answer from step 21, and he shows honor to the one who taught it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer matches step 21 exactly. ריש לקיש was so pleased that he gave רבי ישמעאל בר אבא a seat of honor across from him.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בַּר אַבָּא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael bar Abba said to him:

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי:
phrases.english: This is what Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
As long as it has not carried a load.
He said to him: Sit facing me.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בַּר אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers ריש לקיש's question from step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: As long as it has not carried a load.

steps.title: רבי זירא asks the same question
steps.stepSummary: A second story: רבי זירא sat and wondered how long a camel counts as young.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא was sitting and wondering: until when is a camel young?
steps.whatsHappening: Another short story starts with the same question, this time from רבי זירא. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again no new question is added. It repeats the pattern of the ריש לקיש story, but this story ends very differently.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira was sitting and wondering:
Until when is a camel considered young?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story that follows the pattern of step 25.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The definition of a young camel.

steps.title: רבין בר חיננא answers and keeps repeating it
steps.stepSummary: רבין בר חיננא gives the same answer and keeps repeating it, and רבי זירא teases him for knowing only one teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבין בר חיננא said to him: this is what עולא said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי, as long as it has not carried a load. He kept repeating it. רבי זירא said to him: is this the only thing you have to say?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא gets the same answer, but the man who answered keeps repeating it, and רבי זירא makes a sharp remark.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer matches steps 21 and 26. ריש לקיש honored the one who answered him. רבי זירא instead teased רבין בר חיננא, since repeating one teaching again and again looked like he had nothing else to share.
steps.whatToRemember: The rule is passed down the same way three times: a camel is young as long as it has not carried a load.

phrases.english: Ravin bar Ḥinnana said to him:

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי אָמַר עוּלָּא, אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי:
phrases.english: This is what Ulla said that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
As long as it has not carried a load.
He kept repeating it.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חֲדָא הָוְיָא לָךְ אֲמַרְתְּ.
phrases.english: He said to him: Do you have only one thing to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's question from step 27 and closes the story.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: As long as it has not carried a load.

steps.title: The lesson of the two stories: harsh sages of ארץ ישראל and pious sages of בבל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws a moral from the two camel stories by contrasting the 'harsh' sages of ארץ ישראל with the 'pious' sages of בבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and see the difference between the tough sages of ארץ ישראל and the pious sages of בבל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up the two stories with a short, surprising lesson about how each sage treated the person who taught him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש was known as a tough person, yet he honored רבי ישמעאל בר אבא and seated him facing himself. רבי זירא was known as pious, yet he teased רבין בר חיננא. The point is the irony: the 'harsh' one acted more respectfully than the 'pious' one.
steps.whatToRemember: The camel stories end with a lesson in manners: the 'tough' ריש לקיש honored the one who answered his question, while the 'pious' רבי זירא teased the one who answered his.

phrases.aramaic: תָּא חֲזִי, מָה בֵּין תַּקִּיפֵי אַרְעָא דְיִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: Come and see what the difference is between the harsh ones of the Land of Israel
phrases.notes: The 'harsh one' is ריש לקיש from the first story, and the 'pious one' is רבי זירא from the second.

phrases.english: and the pious ones of Babylonia.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא חֲזִי, מָה בֵּין תַּקִּיפֵי אַרְעָא דְיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a lesson by comparing the two camel stories in steps 25-28.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The 'harsh' sage of ארץ ישראל showed more honor to the one who answered him than the 'pious' sage of בבל did.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: how long is a calf considered young?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about the skin of the head and asks how long a calf counts as 'young.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says 'and the skin of the head,' etc. How long is a calf considered young?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and asks for a definition. This sets up the opinions that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives a special rule for the skin of the head of a 'young calf,' but it never says how old that is. The גמרא wants an exact age, just as the earlier stories asked how long a camel counts as young.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc.: the quote of the משנה continues past these words

phrases.english: And the skin of the head, etc.
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting our משנה, which says the skin of a young calf's head counts like its meat.

phrases.english: And how long is a calf considered young?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the stories and returns to the wording of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The age limit for a calf to count as עגל הרך.

steps.title: עולא says one year, רבי יוחנן says as long as it nurses
steps.stepSummary: Two answers: עולא says a calf is young until it is one year old; רבי יוחנן says it is young for as long as it nurses.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא says: in its first year. רבי יוחנן says: as long as it is nursing.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give different answers to the question of how long a calf counts as young.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא measures by age: the first year. רבי יוחנן measures by the calf's behavior: as long as it still drinks its mother's milk. Since a calf might stop nursing before or after its first birthday, the two answers can give different results.

keyTerms.meaning: In its first year of life

phrases.english: Ulla says: in its first year;

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: כׇּל זְמַן שֶׁיּוֹנֵק.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan says: as long as it is nursing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 30 with two opinions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: עולא: until one year old. רבי יוחנן: as long as it nurses.

steps.title: What exactly did עולא mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how to read עולא: does he mean a calf in its first year that is also still nursing?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: what does עולא mean? A calf in its first year, as long as it is also nursing?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a question about how to understand עולא. Only the first option appears here; the rest of the question continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first option is that עולא needs both things: the calf must be under a year old and also still nursing. If so, a calf that stopped nursing early would no longer count as young. The other option has not been stated yet.

keyTerms.meaning: How does he mean it? What is he saying?

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not finished here. Do not treat 'in its first year and nursing' as עולא's final opinion; it is only the first option.

phrases.english: A dilemma was raised before them: how does Ulla mean it?
In its first year, and only if it is nursing,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks more closely at עולא's answer from step 31.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether עולא requires both conditions (first year and nursing), or something else, which is still to come.
